Since $OB$ passes through the origin $(0, 0)$, its equation is $y = \dfrac{4}{3}x$.
walkthrough:
Reflection makes the symmetry line the perpendicular bisector of the mirrored diagonal.
Calculate gradient and equation of diagonal $AC$:
$$m_{AC} = \dfrac{0 - 6}{8 - 0} = -\dfrac{6}{8} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$
$$y - 6 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 0) \implies y = -\dfrac{3}{4}x + 6$$

Calculate gradient and equation of diagonal $OB$:
$$m_{OB} = -\dfrac{1}{m_{AC}} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$
Since $OB$ passes through $(0, 0)$:
$$y = \dfrac{4}{3}x$$

Reflection makes the symmetry line the perpendicular bisector of the mirrored diagonal.
Equate the two line equations to find the intersection point $M$:
$$\dfrac{4}{3}x = -\dfrac{3}{4}x + 6$$
$$\left(\dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{3}{4}\right)x = 6 \implies \dfrac{25}{12}x = 6 \implies x = \dfrac{72}{25} = 2.88$$
